# watchpoint_service_account (Resource)

A service account: a non-human principal that holds one role and its own API keys. It never counts as a seat and cannot sign in. A key minted for it (a `watchpoint_api_key` with `service_account_id`) can never do more than the role allows, whatever scopes it asks for. Deactivating the account stops its keys at once; deleting it revokes them. Reads need `settings.manage`, writes `apikeys.manage`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A non-human principal for CI, capped by a narrow role, with its own key.
resource "watchpoint_service_account" "ci" {
  name        = "ci-deployer"
  description = "Applies monitoring-as-code from the pipeline"
  role_id     = watchpoint_role.deployer.id
}

resource "watchpoint_api_key" "ci" {
  name               = "ci-deployer"
  service_account_id = watchpoint_service_account.ci.id
  scopes             = ["monitors.write", "checks.run"]
  allowed_ip_ranges  = ["198.51.100.0/24"]
  expires_in_days    = 90
}

output "ci_api_key" {
  value     = watchpoint_api_key.ci.api_key
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Unique name within the tenant (128 characters max).
- `role_id` (String) Role in this tenant that caps everything the account's keys can do.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Optional description.
- `is_active` (Boolean) Whether the account's keys work. Defaults to `true`.

### Read-Only

- `active_key_count` (Number) Number of live keys held by the account.
- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp (RFC 3339).
- `id` (String) Service account ID.
- `role_name` (String) Name of the role, for display.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import watchpoint_service_account.ci sa_001
```
